text:
sara: Quick sync — we need per-GPU caps for max_batch_size and max_tokens_per_batch. Experiments so far show A100/H100 scale linearly but T4/L4 hit a memory frag / KV-eviction regression when tokens_per_batch gets high. Anyone got profiling numbers?

ben: I ran a short suite yesterday on T4/L4/A10/A100. Short summary: T4 starts failing @ ~4k tokens/batch for 8k-seq workloads, memory spikes then KV eviction thrashes. L4 behaves better but kernel selection switches to a slower path for wide batches. A10/A100/H100 look stable up to much larger budgets. :chart_with_upwards_trend:

devin: pasting trimmed profiler output + bench command I used:

```
# command
./bench/continuous_batch.py --model ref-7b --gpu T4 --concurrency 16 --max_tokens_per_batch 8192 --duration 120

\n# perf summary (T4)
p99_latency_ms: 312
p50_latency_ms: 82
throughput_tps: 28
memory_utilization: 0.86
kv_evictions/sec: 4.7
kernel_path: cuBLAS (no flash)

\n# note: kv_evictions spike right before OOMs
```

kai: Helpful. I dug into kernels: T4/L4 fallback to the generic attention kernel when sequence*batches crosses a threshold (we set kernel_switch_tokens=1e6). That threshold is tuned for A100/H100 and is too high for memory-constrained GPUs. Also the token memory cost differs: flash attention path keeps less temporary memory.

ben: From experiments, a simple heuristics we can use:

```
# tokens_per_batch_cap = floor((gpu_usable_mem_bytes * safety_factor) / per_token_mem_bytes)
# safety_factor = 0.75 (empirically stable)
# per_token_mem_bytes approximations:
T4: 120 bytes/token
L4: 90 bytes/token
A10: 70 bytes/token
A100: 40 bytes/token
H100: 35 bytes/token
```

ben: Using that gives reasonable numbers, and we then clamp by an absolute max_batch_size to avoid huge all-to-all overheads.

sara: Can you paste the computed recommendations you used? Want to put them in per-gpu profiles in runtime config.

ben: Yep — these are rounded and include a safety floor for small sequences:

```
# recommended runtime defaults (rounded)
T4: max_batch_size=32, max_tokens_per_batch=4096
L4: max_batch_size=48, max_tokens_per_batch=8192
A10: max_batch_size=64, max_tokens_per_batch=16384
A100: max_batch_size=128, max_tokens_per_batch=32768
H100: max_batch_size=192, max_tokens_per_batch=49152
```

devin: FYI those token caps assume KV caching enabled with prefix reuse. For workloads doing long context without reuse, reduce tokens_per_batch by ~30% (KV growth + temporary activations). Also watch out for multi-instance packing on A10 where 2 processes share one GPU; we should add instance-aware scaling.

kai: One more caveat — kernel selection: if tokens_per_batch is high but sequence length is tiny (e.g., 16 tokens), the token*batches product may still be below kernel_switch_tokens so flash-attn won't be picked. We should add a second heuristic that considers max_seq_len when computing kernel hint.

perf-bot: automated smoke results from canary run (last 30m): A100 canary passed. T4 canary showed 5% p99 regressions when max_tokens_per_batch=8192; failing tests flagged.

sara: Action items:
- ben: add per-GPU profile entries to runtime config with the recommended numbers and include the safety_factor comment.
- devin: update bench harness to run targeted KV-eviction scenarios and log kernel path. Add metrics: kv_evictions/sec, mem_fragmentation_ratio, kernel_path.
- kai: add second heuristic for kernel hint based on max_seq_len.
- ops: run staged canary (5% traffic) for 48h, watch p99, kv_evictions and mem_pressure > 0.8 alerts.

ben: I'll open a PR with the config + unit tests for the heuristic. Will also include a small table in the config comments with the math used to compute recommended caps.

sara: Great. If we see regressions on T4 after deploy we'll lower the T4 caps and re-run the auto-tuner. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
